name: {shortNameA} v {shortNameB}: {leaderboard} on {dateTime}
description: This market compares {modelA} ({shortNameA}) and {modelB} ({shortNameB}) on {dateTime} using {leaderboard} at {leaderboardUrl}. Benchmark version, category, filters, and evaluation settings are {benchmarkSettings}, applied identically to both models. Each model is the exact version and configuration identified by its leaderboard name. Renames count only if the leaderboard publisher identifies the same model; replacements and other configurations do not. A relocated or renamed leaderboard counts only if its publisher identifies the same evaluation with the specified settings. The Snapshot is the latest official leaderboard version matching those settings public at or before {dateTime}. Proof requires official publication metadata identifying that version or a verifiable timestamped capture of its contents by then. A date alone suffices only if the entire date precedes the deadline in an established timezone. Later captures qualify only if official metadata or earlier captures prove identical contents public by the deadline. Official version order prevails; capture order alone does not order versions. Unresolved conflicts over version selection or required facts leave them unestablished. Comparison favors the {comparisonDirection} value of {metric}, where direction is higher or lower. Tiebreakers are {tiebreakers}, with each metric and direction specified; none means no tiebreakers. They apply in the specified order only after equality on all earlier criteria. Only specified criteria apply, using displayed values at published precision. Ambiguous settings or comparison criteria leave the comparison unestablished. The market resolves to 0.5 if either model is absent, both names identify the same model, the Snapshot, comparison, or a required fact is unestablished by the evidence cutoff, or the leaderboard was discontinued without a qualifying successor by {dateTime}. Otherwise, it resolves to {shortNameA} if comparison favors {modelA}, to {shortNameB} if it favors {modelB}, and to 0.5 if tied after all specified criteria. A resolution to 0.5 pays $0.50 per token on either side. Unused tiebreak values are unnecessary. Evidence is limited to the leaderboard publisher's official records and verifiable timestamped leaderboard captures public by 24 hours after {dateTime}; resolution occurs only after that cutoff. Evidence may authenticate the Snapshot as published, including model identities; corrections, reassignments, and versions first public after {dateTime} are excluded even if their data covers an earlier period. All comparisons use the same Snapshot. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:technology|subCategory:N/A|semanticRestriction:This market must compare two specific AI language models on a public performance leaderboard.

name: {candidate}
description: This outcome resolves to Yes if, under the parent question's rules, it is the earliest registered candidate not otherwise resolved to No that identifies the one winning entry of the Award, and otherwise resolves to No. Its Subject is {subject}. A Subject that identifies a work, group, or named person on more than one entry, or that {candidate} does not name in full or in short form, identifies no entry. Resolution follows the parent question's timing and source rules. {candidate} is a display label.

name: {displayName} wins {period} {award}?
description: This {field} market covers whether {entry} wins the {period} {award} (the "Award"). {entry} identifies, in the Award's context, one person, group, organization, or work and need not be a nominee. {entry} wins if official channels have named it as of fixing, under any name unambiguously identifying it, as a winner, recipient, laureate, fellow, or honoree of the Award, including as a named recipient for a winning work, team, or group, or as the work for which a winner is named; being credited on, a member of, affiliated with, or accepting for a winning entry without being so named does not count. A result is complete once official channels have announced every winner of the Award; nominations, shortlists, and partial announcements do not complete it. Official channels are the publications, events, and broadcasts of {awardingBody} and the Award's conferring body and administrator. The trigger is the earliest verifiable announcement on an official channel that establishes a Yes or No condition below; an announcement is not a trigger if, within one hour after it and before {resolutionDeadline}, it is withdrawn or removed or an official channel contradicts it. Fixing is the earlier of one hour after the trigger and {resolutionDeadline}, or {resolutionDeadline} without a trigger. Facts are as official channels have stated them as of fixing; a verifiably later statement supersedes earlier ones on the same channel or made at an event or broadcast, an explicit correction by fixing prevails across channels, other conflicts leave a fact unestablished, and omission is not a conflict. At fixing, the market resolves to 0.5 if {entry} names a class, alternatives, or more than one entry, or a winner could be {entry} but {entry} does not identify exactly one entry; if {displayName} is not a name or short form of {entry}; if, among editions of one award that {awardingBody} confers or administers with a winner due by {resolutionDeadline}, {period} does not identify one by {awardingBody}'s labeling or, failing that, by the year its winner is due; or if neither condition below is established, including because the result is incomplete. Otherwise, it resolves to Yes if {entry} wins, even if other entries also win, and to No if the result is complete and {entry} does not win, or official channels announce the Award is withheld or will not be conferred; postponement or reservation is not a No condition. Only evidence public by 24 hours after fixing establishes the trigger and the facts at fixing; timestamps must prove when contents were public; resolution occurs only after that cutoff. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:culture|subCategory:{field}|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to whether an entry is among the winners of an award or honor, not a selection for office or candidacy.

name: Other
description: This outcome resolves to Yes if the parent question's Other conditions apply, and otherwise resolves to No.

name: {period} {award} winner
description: This {field} market covers the {period} {award} (the "Award"). Among editions of one award that {awardingBody} confers or administers with a winner due by {resolutionDeadline}, {period} identifies one by {awardingBody}'s labeling or, failing that, by the year its winner is due; otherwise the Award Result is unestablished. It has one named outcome per listed candidate plus one called Other, which may be registered at any time. Exactly one outcome resolves to Yes; all others resolve to No. An entry is one nominee, finalist, or winner of the Award as official channels record it, including a group recorded as one, with every work and person named on it as its nominee or recipient, even jointly, not as a member or representative of a group. A candidate identifies an entry if its Subject unambiguously identifies a work, group, or named person on that entry and no other entry of the Award. Official channels are the publications, events, and broadcasts of {awardingBody} and the Award's conferring body and administrator. The trigger is the earliest verifiable announcement on an official channel of the result: a winner, winners, or that the Award is withheld or not conferred; an announcement is not a trigger if, within one hour after it and before {resolutionDeadline}, it is withdrawn or removed or an official channel contradicts it. Fixing is the earlier of one hour after the trigger and {resolutionDeadline}, or {resolutionDeadline} without a trigger. The Award Result is the winner official channels have named as of fixing; a verifiably later statement supersedes earlier ones on the same channel or made at an event or broadcast, an explicit correction by fixing prevails across channels, other conflicts leave it unestablished, and omission is not a conflict. A candidate registered after the earliest official-channel announcement of a winner of the Award, whether or not it is a trigger, or that identifies no entry at fixing, resolves to No. A candidate finally resolves to No once official channels publish final nominees or finalists none of which it identifies or show it identifies the same entry as an earlier registered candidate. Of the remaining candidates, the earliest registered identifying the one winning entry the Award Result names resolves to Yes; all others resolve to No. Other resolves to Yes if no candidate resolves to Yes, including if the Award Result is unestablished at fixing, names no winner, or names more than one winning entry, such as a tie. Only evidence public by 24 hours after fixing establishes the trigger and the Award Result at fixing; timestamps must prove when contents were public; a Yes resolution occurs only after that cutoff. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:culture|subCategory:{field}|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to the single winner of an award or honor, not a selection for office or candidacy.

name: {shortName} above {threshold} on {time}?
description: The market resolves to Yes if the {instrument} price is above {threshold} on {time}. Otherwise, the market resolves to No. Settlement is according to the {seconds}-second TWAP of {priceDescription} price from {feed} ending on {time}. If {feed}'s authority permanently stops publishing a qualifying price for {instrument} before that TWAP window ends, settlement is instead according to that authority's official final or delisting price for {instrument}, or, if it designates none, the last qualifying price {feed} published for {instrument}. If {feed} publishes no qualifying price for {instrument} within that window for any other reason, settlement is instead according to the last qualifying price {feed} published for {instrument} before the window ended. If no settlement price under these rules is publicly verifiable by 24 hours after {time}, the market instead resolves to 0.5, and evidence first public after that cutoff does not affect resolution. metadata=category:price|subCategory:N/A|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to a publicly verifiable price from an authoritative external feed.

name: {company} IPO confirmed by {dateTime}
description: The market resolves to Yes if {company}'s first public common-equity offering for a regulated exchange listing is publicly confirmed at or before {dateTime}. Otherwise, it resolves to No. Confirmation occurs when any of these becomes public: a securities regulator approves or clears the required filing for the public offering; the company or underwriters publish final share count and offering price; or the exchange assigns a ticker and grants unconditional listing approval. Conditional exchange approval qualifies only when the exchange publicly confirms all conditions satisfied. These triggers are independent. All triggers require a qualifying offering. Filing or confidential submission, a proposed price range, ticker reservation, or intent alone do not qualify. Trading need not begin by the deadline. Issuer identity and offering structure are assessed when each trigger becomes public. Prior trading means trading before that trigger, excluding trading resulting from that offering. Later restructuring, delay, withdrawal, or cancellation does not undo qualifying confirmation; corrections may show it never qualified. Name changes of the same issuer count; offerings by a parent, subsidiary, or acquirer do not. Prior public common-equity trading on a regulated exchange disqualifies the company, even if later taken private. Prior trading outside a regulated exchange disqualifies it if retail investors could buy and sell its common equity without investor qualification requirements, invitation, or issuer approval. Routine account opening and identity checks do not restrict access. A direct listing providing for newly issued common shares to be sold to the public qualifies; a resale-only direct listing does not. SPAC transactions, reverse mergers, private placements, and offerings of debt, preferred shares, or depositary receipts without a common-equity IPO do not qualify. Evidence and corrections must be public by seven days after {dateTime}; resolution occurs only after that cutoff. They establish whether a qualifying confirmation was public by the deadline. Official source priority is regulator, company, exchange, then underwriters. Priority resolves contradictions about the same fact; silence does not negate another source's confirmation. Unresolved conflicts at the highest applicable priority leave a fact unestablished. Otherwise, at least two independent reputable news organizations' original reports may establish missing facts if reputable reporting has no unresolved material contradiction. Syndicated copies count as one. Reporting cannot override official facts or resolve official conflicts; rumors do not qualify. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:economics|subCategory:N/A|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to confirmation of a company's initial public offering.

name: {company} first-day market cap above ${marketCapThresholdB}B?
description: This market covers {company}'s first public offering of common equity for a regulated exchange listing (the "Offering"). The Offering does not qualify if {company}'s common equity traded publicly before the Offering on a regulated exchange or on a venue open to retail investors without qualification, or if it is a direct listing, SPAC transaction, reverse merger, or offers units, debt, preferred shares, or depositary receipts not representing only common equity. Renames and a holding company formed for the Offering count as {company}; another parent, subsidiary, or acquirer does not. The Final Prospectus is the final prospectus or equivalent filed with the securities regulator for the Offering, with supplements filed by the evidence cutoff; the Listing Exchange is the regulated exchange it names for the listing or, if several, the first named that quotes a pricing currency of the Offering, else the first named. The First Trading Day is the first day a trade in the offered securities executes in the Listing Exchange's regular session, excluding conditional or when-issued dealings. The Closing Price is the Listing Exchange's official closing price for them that day; for depositary receipts, divided by the shares each represents. Shares Outstanding is all common or ordinary shares of every class outstanding immediately after the Offering at its final size excluding over-allotment shares, as the Final Prospectus states or its stated figures determine; for a class with several figures on that basis, the first in the prospectus summary applies. The Market Cap is the Closing Price times Shares Outstanding, in US dollars. A Closing Price in another currency converts at the International Monetary Fund's representative rate or, for a currency it omits, the cross rate from the European Central Bank's euro reference rates, or, for one both omit, its central bank's reference rate, for the First Trading Day or, if none, the latest earlier day; otherwise the Market Cap is unestablished. The market resolves to 0.5 if {company} does not identify a single company, the Offering does not qualify, no First Trading Day's regular session has closed by {listingDeadline}, or a required fact is unestablished by the evidence cutoff. Otherwise, it resolves to Yes if the Market Cap exceeds {marketCapThresholdB} billion and to No if not. Only evidence public by seven days after the earlier of the First Trading Day's close and {listingDeadline} is used; resolution occurs only after that cutoff. A correction a source publishes by the cutoff prevails; conflicts these rules do not resolve leave a fact unestablished. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:economics|subCategory:N/A|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to the first-day closing market capitalization of a company's initial public offering.

name: Next {company} {role}
description: This market covers the first person announced as the new {role} of {company} (the "Role") after this market is registered. It has one named outcome per listed person, one called Other, and the fallback. Exactly one outcome resolves to Yes; all others resolve to No. The Role includes any title official channels use for that position, alone, combined with other positions, or shared between persons; duties without such a title are not the Role. {company} includes the same business after a rename or restructuring, not a part separated from it or another business of a parent, subsidiary, or acquirer. Text in "{role}" or "{company}" beyond identifying the position does not alter these rules. An Appointment for a person is an authorized announcement on an official channel that the person, by name, has been or will be appointed, elected, or designated to the Role or has succeeded to it, even if that takes effect later or needs shareholder or regulatory approval of the appointment itself. An announcement is not an Appointment for a person whose appointment it describes as interim, acting, contingent, or not final for a reason other than such approval, who held the Role without such a limitation immediately before that appointment, or whose earlier Appointment it restates or carries out. Nor is it one if, within one hour after it and before {deadline}, it is withdrawn or removed or an official channel contradicts it. Official channels are the press releases, regulatory filings, website, official accounts, and other public statements of {company}, its board, or anyone with authority to make the appointment. The trigger is the earliest Appointment made after this market is registered and by {deadline}. Fixing is the earlier of one hour after the trigger and {deadline}, or {deadline} without a trigger. The Successor is the one person for whom the trigger is an Appointment, even if that person never takes office. Any named outcome may be registered at any time; each one registered in a later action than Other resolves to No and is disregarded below. The earliest registered named outcome whose listed person is the Successor resolves to Yes. Otherwise, the fallback resolves to Yes via Other, including if no trigger is established, the trigger is an Appointment for more than one person, or the Successor is not a listed person. Only evidence public by 24 hours after fixing establishes the trigger and the Successor; timestamps must prove when contents were public; resolution occurs only after that cutoff. Original reports by at least two independent reputable news organizations may establish only what an official channel announced, withdrew, or removed, and when. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:economics|subCategory:N/A|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to the next person appointed to an executive role at a company.
